Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:10:1.hebrew: או דילמא כי כתיב - "גאולתו" בשדה אחוזתו, למעט חצאין הוא דכתיב, שנאמר (שם) "ומצא כדי גאולתו" — כדי כולו, ולא כדי חציו. הילכך, כי חזר כתב ג"ש, למגמר אחדא מילתא הוא דכתיב, ולא למיגמר גאולת קרובים, דלאו לגבי גאולתו כתיבי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:10:1.english: Or perhaps, when it is written - "its redemption" in the case of the ancestral field, it is written to exclude partial [redemption], as it says (there) "and he finds sufficient for its redemption" — sufficient for all of it, and not sufficient for half of it. Therefore, when [the Torah] repeated and wrote [the word] as a verbal analogy (gezeira shava), it was written to teach about that one matter [the exclusion of partial redemption], and not to teach about the redemption by relatives, since [those verses] are not written with regard to its redemption.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:11:1.hebrew: בכל גאולה תתנו - "ובכל ארץ אחוזתכם גאולה תתנו לארץ". קרא יתירא הוא, ולא פירש למאי אתא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:11:1.english: "In all [of it] you shall grant redemption" - "And in all the land of your possession you shall grant redemption for the land." The verse is superfluous, and it did not explain for what [purpose] it came:

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:11:2.hebrew: לרבות בתים ועבד עברי - שיהו נגאלין לקרובים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:11:2.english: To include houses and a Hebrew slave - That they may be redeemed by relatives.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:11:3.hebrew: בתי החצרים - עיירות שאין מוקפות חומה מימות יהושע:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:11:3.english: Houses of the courtyards - Towns that have not been surrounded by a wall since the days of Joshua.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:12:1.hebrew: על שדה הארץ יחשב - הרי הן כשדה אחוזה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:12:1.english: “With the field of the country shall it be reckoned” - Behold, they are like an ancestral field.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:12:2.english: To establish it as an obligation - upon the relatives.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:13:1.hebrew: וכי יש לך אדם בישראל - מנוטלי חלק בארץ, שאין לו גואלין מזרע יעקב, בעוד אחד מכל ישראל קיים הוא קרוב לו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:13:1.english: But is there a man among you in Israel - from among those who received a portion in the Land, who has no redeemers from the seed of Jacob? As long as one person from all of Israel survives, he is a relative of his:

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:13:2.hebrew: אלא יש לו - גואלין, אבל אין הגואל רוצה ליקח; ולימדך הכתוב שהרשות ביד הקרוב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:13:2.english: Rather, one who has - redeemers, but the redeemer does not want to purchase; and the verse taught you that the option is in the hand of the relative.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:13:3.hebrew: אלא יש לו - גואלין, אבל אין הגואל רוצה ליקח, ולימדך הכתוב שהרשות ביד הקרוב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:13:3.english: Rather, he has - redeemers, but the redeemer does not want to buy [the field], and the verse teaches you that the option is in the hand of the relative.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:14:1.hebrew: חובה - והאי "כי לא יהיה לו גואל" דריש בשאי אפשר ביד הראוי ליורשו ליגאל, ואין הגאולה מוטלת אלא על הקרוב מן הכל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:14:1.english: An obligation - And this [verse], "If he has no redeemer," he expounds as referring to a case where it is impossible for the one fit to inherit him to redeem, and the redemption is incumbent only on the closest of all [relatives]:

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:15:1.english: What is “in all”? - Let [the Torah] write “you shall grant a redemption for the land.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:16:1.hebrew: מה ת"ל - בעבד עברי הנמכר לעובד כוכבים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:16:1.english: What does the verse state - Regarding a Hebrew slave who was sold to a gentile:

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:16:2.hebrew: לרבות כל הגאולות - כל הגאולות העומדות ליגאל, שיהא נגאל כסדר הזה. קס"ד שיהו נגאלין לקרובים, בא ללמדנו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:16:2.english: To include all redemptions - [All the redemptions] that are destined to be redeemed, that [the property] be redeemed in this order. The Gemara's initial thought is that [the verse] comes to teach us that they are redeemed by relatives.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:16:3.hebrew: ועבד עברי - הנמכר לישראל, דלא כתיב ביה גאולת קרובים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:16:3.english: And a Hebrew slave - One who is sold to a Jew, for [the law of] redemption by relatives is not written regarding him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:17:1.hebrew: לקרוב קרוב קודם - דגבי שדה אחוזה כתי' ובא גואלו הקרוב אליו, ולא פי' הקרוב קרוב קודם כי הכא דפריש דודו ברישא, ואם אין לו דוד — בן דודו, ואי לאו — משאר בשרו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:17:1.english: The closer one [is] first - For regarding an ancestral field it is written, "And his redeemer who is close to him shall come" (Leviticus 25:25), and it does not specify [who is] the closer, [so that the] closer is first, as it does here, where it specifies his uncle first; and if he has no uncle, his uncle's son; and if not, [one] of his [other] close relatives.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:18:1.hebrew: ועבד עברי - הנמכר לישראל, דלא כתיב ביה גאולת קרובים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:18:1.english: And a Hebrew slave - One who is sold to a Jew, for [the verse] does not write about him redemption by relatives.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:18:2.hebrew: מי שאינו נגאל באלה נגאל בשש - אלמא ס"ל דאין נגאל בקרובים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:18:2.english: One who is not redeemed by these is redeemed by six - Evidently, he holds that [a Hebrew slave sold to a gentile] is not redeemed by relatives.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:19:1.hebrew: יגאלנו - כתיב בנמכר לעובד כוכבים גבי קרובים, ומשמע מיעוטא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:19:1.english: “May redeem him” - [This] is written regarding one sold to a gentile, in the context of relatives, and it implies a limitation:

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:1:1.hebrew: הא רבנן - דלא יהבי טעמא לקרא, ואמרי דהורע כחו בחדא מילתא — הורע נמי במילתא אחריתא, בר מהיכא דגלי ביה קרא. ובבתי ערי חומה גמרינן גאולה גאולה משדה אחוזה. והא דקא אמינא דבית בעיר חומה לוה וגואל כו' — לר"ש קאמינא, דיהיב טעמא לקרא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:1:1.english: This is [according to] the Rabbis - Who do not give a reason for the verse, and they say that if his power was weakened in one matter, it is weakened also in another matter, except where the verse revealed otherwise. And with regard to houses in walled cities, we derive [the law] by analogy of "redemption" "redemption" from an ancestral field. And as for what I said that a house in a walled city, [one] borrows and redeems, etc. — I said it according to Rabbi Shimon, who does give a reason for the verse.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:20:1.hebrew: לרבות בתים ועבד עברי - שיהו נגאלין לקרובים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:20:1.english: To include houses and a Hebrew slave - That they may be redeemed by relatives.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:2:1.hebrew: תני חדא - ברייתא אחת שנשנית על המוכר בית בעיר חומה: לוה וגואל כו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:2:1.english: One [baraita] taught - Regarding one who sells a house in a walled city: He may borrow and redeem, etc.:

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:4:1.hebrew: איכא למיפרך - בהא מתניתין, דאצרכה קרא למקדיש שילוה ויגאל, משום דהא אתיא ליה מדינא של מוכר בית בעיר חומה שאין לוה וגואל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:4:1.english: There is [room] to refute - In this Mishnah, for which Scripture was needed [to teach] that one who consecrates [a field] may borrow [the money] and redeem [it], because [otherwise] it would come to him from the law of one who sells a house in a walled city, who may not borrow and redeem:

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:4:2.english: What [is unique] about one who sells a house in a walled city, that his power to redeem forever was diminished - From after the first year onward.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:4:3.hebrew: תאמר במקדיש שיפה כחו לגאול לעולם - לעולמו של יובל, אם לא מכרה הגזבר, דאין השדה מתחלקת לכהנים עד היובל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:4:3.english: Shall you say with regard to one who consecrates [a field], whose power is enhanced to redeem forever - [Forever means] until the Jubilee, if the treasurer has not sold it, for [the field] is not distributed to the priests until the Jubilee:

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:6:1.hebrew: אף אני אביא מקדיש - לפיכך הוצרך הכתוב אם גאל יגאל לומר שלוה וגואל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:6:1.english: I will also bring one who consecrates - Therefore, it was necessary [for the verse] to say "if he will redeem, he shall redeem" to teach that one may borrow and redeem.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:7:1.hebrew: איכא למיפרך - בהא מתניתין, דאצרכה קרא למקדיש שילוה ויגאל, משום דהא אתיא ליה מדינא של מוכר בית בעיר חומה, שאין לוה וגואל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:7:1.english: It can be refuted - With regard to this Mishnah, that the verse was needed [to teach] that one who consecrates [his field] may borrow and redeem [it], because [otherwise] this would come to him from the law of one who sells a house in a walled city, [where] he does not borrow and redeem.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:7:2.hebrew: בשנה שניה - דמוכר שדה אחוזה אין המוכר יכול לגאול עד שתבוא שנה שלישית, ומוכר בית בעיר חומה אינו גואל אלא בראשונה. נמצא שאין זה וזה גואלין בשניה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:7:2.english: In the second year - For one who sells an ancestral field, the seller cannot redeem it until the third year comes; and one who sells a house in a walled city redeems it only in the first year. It turns out that neither this one nor that one redeems in the second year.

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:8:1.hebrew: עבד עברי וכו' - כדאמר לעיל (קידושין דף כ:): ונגאל כולו ולא לחציו, ואין לוה וגואל, דהא "או השיגה" כתיב (ויקרא כה):
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:8:1.english: A Hebrew slave, etc. - As stated above (Kiddushin 20b): "And he is redeemed entirely, but not partially," and he cannot borrow and redeem himself, for it is written "or he attains [the means]" (Leviticus 25):

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:9:1.hebrew: נגאל בקרובים - על כרחו של לוקח, כדאשכחן בשדה אחוזה (שם): ובא גואלו הקרוב אליו וגו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:9:1.english: Is redeemed by relatives - Against the will of the buyer, as we find with an ancestral field (there, Leviticus 25:25): "And his redeemer who is near to him shall come, etc."

Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:9:2.hebrew: אף האי נמי אין נגאל לחצאין - לרבנן קבעי ליה, דאמרי לעיל אין נגאל לחצאין, ונימא נמי דלהכי גמר דנגאל בקרובים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 21a:9:2.english: So too, this one also cannot be redeemed partially - He is asking this according to the Rabbis, who said above that [a house] cannot be redeemed partially; and let us also say that for this reason [the verse] derived that it can be redeemed by relatives.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 21a:15:1.hebrew: מאי בכל - היה לו לכתוב "גאולה תתנו לארץ", ושמעינן מזה שדה אחוזה, לקובעו חובה, ובתי החצרים בכלל. וא"ת: לימא דאתי לרבות עבד עברי? ויש לומר: דמשמע ליה דאתי לרבויי מידי דגאולת קרקע, כדכתיב "ובכל ארץ" — משמע דוקא ארץ מרבינן:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 21a:15:1.english: What is [the meaning of] "in all" - [The verse] should have written, "you shall grant a redemption for the land," and we would have understood from this [the law of] an ancestral field, establishing it as an obligation, and the houses of the unwalled villages would be included. And if you ask: Let us say that ["in all"] comes to include a Hebrew slave? One can answer: He understood that it comes to include something pertaining to the redemption of land, as it is written, "and in all the land" — which implies that we include only land:

Tosafot on Kiddushin 21a:8:1.hebrew: משום דאיכא למימר ע"ע הנמכר לעובד כוכבים יוכיח - וא"ת: ולמה לי "ומצא כדי גאולתו" דכתיב בשדה אחוזה למימר שאינו גואל לחצאין? תיפוק ליה בק"ו מע"ע: ומה ע"ע הנמכר לעובד כוכבים שיפה כחו ליגאל מיד, ואפ"ה אינו לוה וגואל וגואל לחצאין, כדבסמוך — מוכר שדה אחוזה שהורע כחו, ליגאל מיד, כדכתיב במספר שני תבואות (ויקרא כ״ה:ט״ו), אין דין שאין לוה וגואל וגואל לחצאין? וי"ל דאדרבה אית לן למימר איפכא: ומה מקדיש שהורע כחו ליחלק לכהנים ביובל, ואפ"ה לוה וגואל וגואל לחצאין, מוכר שיפה כחו שחוזרת לבעלים ביובל אינו דין שלוה וגואל וגואל לחצאין? וכ"ת: מה למקדיש שיפה כחו ליגאל מיד, תאמר במוכר שהורע כחו ליגאל מיד? מ"מ בתי החצרים שיפה כחן ליגאל מיד מצינו למיגמר מהאי ק"ו, ולהיות לוה וגואל וגואל לחצאין. ומאחר דחזינן בבתי החצרים, שדה אחוזה נמי מפקי' ליה להאי דינא, דתרוייהו בחד פרש' כתיבי: "על שדה הארץ יחשב". ולהכי איצטריך "ומצא כדי גאולתו" דכתיב במוכר שדה אחוזה, לומר שאינו לוה וגואל וגואל לחצאין, דס"ד למילף ממקדיש כדפרישית, ומהשתא ילפינן נמי בתי החצרים מיניה שאין לוה וגואל וגואל לחצאין:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 21a:8:1.english: Because it can be said, "A Hebrew slave sold to a gentile can prove [otherwise]" - And if you ask: Why do I need "and he finds enough for his redemption," which is written regarding a field of inheritance, to say that one may not redeem partially? Let it be derived by an a fortiori argument from the Hebrew slave: If a Hebrew slave sold to a gentile, whose power is enhanced to be redeemed immediately, nevertheless may not borrow and redeem or redeem partially, as [stated] shortly below — then a seller of a field of inheritance, whose power is diminished [in that he cannot] redeem immediately, as it is written regarding the number of crop years (Leviticus 25:15), is it not logical that he may not borrow and redeem or redeem partially? And one can answer: On the contrary, we could say the opposite: If one who consecrates [a field], whose power is diminished in that it is divided among the priests at the Jubilee, nevertheless may borrow and redeem and redeem partially, then a seller, whose power is enhanced in that it returns to its owners at the Jubilee, is it not logical that he may borrow and redeem and redeem partially? And if you say: What of the one who consecrates, whose power is enhanced in that he can redeem immediately — would you say the same of a seller, whose power is diminished [in that he cannot] redeem immediately? In any case, regarding houses of the courtyards, whose power is enhanced to be redeemed immediately, we find that we can derive from this a fortiori argument that one may borrow and redeem and redeem partially. And since we see this in houses of the courtyards, we would also remove this law from a field of inheritance, for both are written in one passage: "It shall be reckoned as the field of the land." And therefore "and he finds enough for his redemption," which is written regarding the seller of a field of inheritance, is needed, to say that he may not borrow and redeem or redeem partially, since one might have thought to derive [the law] from the one who consecrates, as I explained; and from now on we also derive houses of the courtyards from it, that one may not borrow and redeem or redeem partially:
